policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'there is no unrighteousness in him' renders the noun 'iniquity/unrighteousness' that both the qere עַוְלָתָה and the ketiv עלתה (the same word in defective spelling, or at most a vowelless form the English cannot separate) yield; no italic supply and no ASV note on the verse. The English does not distinguish the spellings, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
